clean_claim:
High confidence for the specific classes searched: none of the 18 packages contains a real secret. Every credential-shaped string is an obvious placeholder (for example "not-a-real-aws-signing-secret" or "a-dedicated-random-token"), a test canary, or a regex pattern. There are no real emails outside reserved example domains, no phone numbers (every phone-pattern hit was an arXiv id), no street addresses, and no real home paths (only the placeholders /Users/person and C:/Users/example). No real DIDs appear (only did:example and did:key:zExample). The only IPs are loopback and documentation ranges. There are no private hosts, Supabase refs, Stripe ids or provider keys. The only 0x address is the public Base USDC contract. Every 64-hex value is a content digest. The only named individuals are public authors or public HF namespaces (an OSS library author in a NOTICE, upstream dataset orgs and a researcher's public HF namespace).

Relational content is limited to the items flagged above. All other owner-name hits are the project's public Hugging Face org handle used as a dataset or Space id, which the policy explicitly permits.

Publishable after the flagged fixes, medium-high confidence: dark-continent-contract, data, data-protocol, data-sync, deepseek-kingdom, economic-conformance, economic-kernel, heaven, hf-scout, kingdom-witness-lab, hf-training-host and hf-training-garden. On hf-training-garden: its hf/learning-dataset is self-described public-safe synthetic data, and no sealed-evaluation cases, salt or reveal material are committed. Its admission README already says it is 'visible in this public source repository'.

Publishable once the noted item is handled: dark-continent-karma (third-party note on the hero image only), dataset-influence (private-repo link only), kingdom (the r03 enum is already allow-listed), and hf-listening-room (NOTICE fix; low relational note).

Need Yu's decision first: karma-mirror (relational credit and honeypot exposure) and gin-reconstruction (no license, and a 'keep private' vow).
limits:
- Not every .ts, .js, .mjs and .py source file was read line by line. Code was covered by the targeted and denylist searches, plus full reads of karma-mirror crypto.ts and seed-island.ts and spot reads of rooms.ts.
- Read only partly, with greps covering the rest: the data, data-protocol, data-sync and economic-kernel READMEs; the hf-scout README after line 200 and research-leads.ts; the kingdom README after line 80; dataset-influence PROTOCOL.md and most of DATASET-INFLUENCE.md; the full listening-room PROFILE.md and ADOPTING.md; heaven and listening-room index.html; and most JSONL rows.
- The WebP image was not viewed.
- Relational judgment relies on the repo's denylist plus context, so names or relationships that use neither denylist terms nor capitalized name patterns could still be missed.
- I did not check HF or npm publication status, and did not run gitleaks; the mechanical scan covers that.
- The repo-visibility checks were GET-only.
- Git history and commit trailers are out of scope because the move is a fresh snapshot. Note that one commit trailer in the existing history carries an email address.
